origin.description: Returns a theoretical Lorenz curve for one income distribution, with its parameters held fixed.

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: Income distribution. One of Singh-Maddala, Dagum, lognorm, Pareto, or exponential. A unique prefix is enough, and the default is Singh-Maddala.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.text: Parameter value or values for that distribution. The exponential curve does not use this argument.

origin.details: The result is a function of class theorLc. Evaluating it at population shares gives the Lorenz ordinates of the chosen distribution. The five choices are the Singh-Maddala, Dagum, lognormal, Pareto, and exponential curves.

translation.description: Returns a theoretical Lorenz curve for one income distribution, with its parameters held fixed.

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: Income distribution. One of Singh-Maddala, Dagum, lognorm, Pareto, or exponential. A unique case-sensitive prefix is enough. The default is Singh-Maddala.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.text: Parameter value or values closed over by the returned curve. A number or a sequence is accepted. The exponential branch ignores it.

translation.details: The call returns a function of the population share only. Singh-Maddala, Dagum, lognorm, and Pareto forward to the matching curve with the captured parameter. Exponential always evaluates the parameter-free curve.
translation.value: A callable f(p). Its values are a NumPy array of the same shape as p.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from ineq.theor import theorLc

p = np.arange(1, 11) / 10
mydagum = theorLc(type="Dagum", parameter=(3.4, 2.6))
print(mydagum(p))
